#+title: Constellation — the repos around the monorepo
#+startup: showall
#+options: toc:nil num:nil
# generated by `bb devtour` from docs/devtour/tour.edn — do not edit

graphden is one of seven repositories, and the seams the other six plug into all live here: addon config fragments, the capability predicates, the external-package manifest, and a CI guard for the vars a private repo reaches. This block tours those seams and tells the other side of each — what graphden-cloud, graphden-tenancy, graphden-mathx, graphden-examples, graphden-internal and the org ~.github~ repo contribute, how they pin each other, and how a release moves through all of them.

after: boot, packages, platform

* 1. addon-config-resources
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: constellation/addon-config-resources
:FILE: src/graphden/system/config.clj
:LINE: 57
:MINS: 1.4
:END:

The whole open-core split hangs off ONE environment variable. Core runs as-is with it unset (single-tenant, every seam at its default). Production sets ~GRAPHDEN_ADDON_CONFIGS=graphden/tenancy/addon.edn,cloud/addon.edn,cloud/prod.edn~ — three classpath resources from two OTHER repos, applied in order. The map of the constellation, and the direction of every arrow: *graphden-cloud* depends on *graphden-tenancy* and *graphden*; tenancy depends on graphden; graphden depends only on *graphden-mathx*. Nothing public ever depends on anything private, and nothing depends on graphden-cloud.

* 2. merge-addon
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: constellation/merge-addon
:FILE: src/graphden/system/config.clj
:LINE: 68
:MINS: 1.9
:END:

How a fragment attaches: its ~:graphden/require~ directive loads the addon's namespaces (so their ~ig/init-key~ defmethods exist — tenancy registers about twenty-five: ~:org/scoped-storage~, ~:tenancy/request-scope~, ~:tenancy/execute-guard~, ~:auth/multi-tenant-provider~, ~:tenancy/app-router~, …), then the rest deep-merges over the core config. graphden-tenancy is a pure source library (33 namespaces under ~graphden.tenancy.*~, hub ~addon.clj~, plus the ~tenancy-admin~ package — deliberately NOT depending on ~app~); graphden-cloud adds only three more namespaces (usage metering, a quota execute-guard, a db helper) and the ~landing~ package that IS graphden.dev's own site. The rule in docs/PACKAGE_DISTRIBUTION.md § 16: cloud vs self-hosted is a MODE of one binary, never a fork.

* 3. install-org-cap-fn!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: constellation/install-org-cap-fn!
:FILE: src/graphden/tenancy/context.clj
:LINE: 130
:MINS: 1.3
:END:

The only policy seam core exposes as a mutable slot. ~graphden.tenancy.context~ is the ONE tenancy namespace kept in this repo: the ~*current-org*~ thread-local, the tier predicates, and two default-deny capability predicates the addon installs at boot (~addon.clj~ calls this with ~org-admin/current-has-org-capability?~ and its platform twin with ~grant/current-has-platform-capability?~). Every authz gate in core reads through them — so a self-hosted instance denies nothing and a cloud instance denies by grant, from the same call sites. docs/TENANCY_SEAM.md is the mechanism half; the policy half's ADRs live in the private repo's ~docs/PLATFORM_NOTES.md~.

…and the one fact server-rendered copy is allowed to branch on: is the addon installed at all. Not a config flag, not a tier — the installed predicate itself. The editor derives the same answer from capability headers, so nothing is duplicated client-side; a page that says 'organisation' only when there are organisations gets it from here.

The guard that makes a private consumer safe to have. Most vars the tenancy addon reaches have NO caller in graphden — they exist for the addon — so a refactor here can drop one and this suite stays green; the break would surface at pin-bump time in a repo this CI cannot see (it did: splitting ~crud/entities.clj~ lost ~view-impl-filter~). ~tools/open-core-seam.edn~ lists every such var, generated from the addon's own requires, and this test resolves each one. Rename or move one → red HERE, in the same landing.

* 6. read-manifest

:CUSTOM_ID: constellation/read-manifest
:FILE: src/graphden/packages/manifest.clj

The other kind of sibling: an external Type-2 package (code + fn-defs in its own repo). ~resources/executor-packages.edn~ is the operator's single data file naming them — today exactly one, *graphden-mathx* (~:gcd~ + ~:gcd-with-12~, the smallest package that proves the path end-to-end). ~build.clj~ bundles the listed libs into the uberjar; ~:app/packages~ loads them by name at boot. A name-only entry means the package is already on the classpath by other means.

:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: constellation/extra-deps
:FILE: src/graphden/packages/manifest.clj

Where the manifest meets tools.deps. The ~{lib coord}~ map the build basis adds — and the reason ~bb pkg-pin-sync~ exists: ~deps.edn~ and the manifest must name the same ~:git/sha~, or the lint/test classpath and the shipped jar disagree. Its sibling ~bb pkg-copy-sync~ guards CONTENT: ~external-packages/{mathx,examples}~ are plain in-tree copies (no submodules — § 15 AD-3) that ~:override-deps~ / the test paths actually exercise, checked byte-identical against the standalone checkouts when they are present. *graphden-examples* rides only that way — 28 lesson modules on the dev/test path, never in a production graph.

* 8. -main
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: constellation/-main
:FILE: src/graphden/executor_runtime/core.clj
:LINE: 187
:MINS: 2.1
:END:

Same ~-main~, second reading: graphden-cloud's ~:run~ alias starts THIS namespace — it ships no main of its own — and its Dockerfile pins the same JRE digest as ours. The release train (~bb release~ in graphden-cloud, every step idempotent): bump tenancy's graphden pin → push tenancy ~main~ → wait for its CI on the self-hosted runner → bump both pins in cloud → regenerate the baked tutorial → assert the *pin diamond* is closed (cloud and tenancy must name ONE graphden sha, or prod runs tenancy against a graphden it was never tested on; checked again in ~deploy.yml~) → push, and the push to cloud ~main~ IS the prod deploy → fast-forward this repo's public ~main~ and tag ~prod-<stamp>~. The two repos without code edges: *graphden-internal* (private planning, legal, the RU translations of the tutorial and of THIS tour — its bake re-invokes our ~bb devtour~ — and the CI-runner setup) and *graphden-dotgithub* (org-level issue / PR templates, no reusable workflows). ~graphden-wt/~ beside them is not a repo but the worktree root the merge queue parks agents in (dev/wtq/).
